{{Elections in Mississippi}}
The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Mississippi''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the four [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Mississippi]], one from each of the state's four [[Mississippi's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[2022 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2022 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]].

{{seealso|Mississippi's 1st congressional district}}
The 1st district takes in the northeastern area of the state, including [[Columbus, Mississippi|Columbus]], [[Oxford, Mississippi|Oxford]], [[Southaven, Mississippi|Southaven]], and [[Tupelo, Mississippi|Tupelo]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Trent Kelly]], who was re-elected with 68.7% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT">{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Cheryl L.|title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 3, 2020|url=http://history.house.gov/Institution/Election-Statistics/Election-Statistics/|publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives|Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives]]|date=February 28, 2019}}</ref>

{{seealso|Mississippi's 2nd congressional district}}
The 2nd district encompasses the [[Mississippi Delta]], taking in most of [[Jackson, Mississippi|Jackson]], the riverfront cities of [[Greenville, Mississippi|Greenville]] and [[Vicksburg, Mississippi|Vicksburg]], and the interior market cities of [[Clarksdale, Mississippi|Clarksdale]], [[Greenwood, Mississippi|Greenwood]] and [[Clinton, Mississippi|Clinton]]. The incumbent is Democrat [[Bennie Thompson]], who was re-elected with 66.0% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT"/>

{{seealso|Mississippi's 3rd congressional district}}
The 3rd district is located in eastern and southwestern Mississippi, taking in [[Meridian, Mississippi|Meridian]], [[Starkville, Mississippi|Starkville]], [[Pearl, Mississippi|Pearl]], [[Natchez, Mississippi|Natchez]], and most of the wealthier portions of [[Jackson, Mississippi|Jackson]], including the portion of the city located in [[Rankin County, Mississippi|Rankin County]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Michael Guest (politician)|Michael Guest]], who was elected with 64.7% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT"/>

The 4th district encompasses the [[Mississippi Gulf Coast]], including [[Gulfport, MS|Gulfport]], [[Biloxi, MS|Biloxi]], [[Hattiesburg, MS|Hattiesburg]], [[Bay St. Louis, MS|Bay St. Louis]], [[Laurel, MS|Laurel]], and [[Pascagoula, MS|Pascagoula]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Steven Palazzo]], who was re-elected unopposed in 2020.<ref name="HPVT"/>
